title: shelf-life of developer and bleach chemicals

posts.topic_title: shelf-life of developer and bleach chemicals
posts.author: John CK
posts.post_subject: shelf-life of developer and bleach chemicals
posts.content_md: Is there any place where I could find out the shelf-life for the various bulk chemicals I use in developing and bleaching? I know some are very stable, but others such as mitol, Pinacyanol or silver nitrate I am not so sure of. I am suprised at how many chemicals I have aquired for this hobby!

posts.topic_title: shelf-life of developer and bleach chemicals
posts.author: Dinesh
posts.post_subject: shelf-life of developer and bleach chemicals
posts.content_md:
You could try the MSDS for the particular chemical. Most of them are available on-line. Here, for instance, is the MSDS for Silver Nitrate: [http://www.jtbaker.com/msds/englishhtml/s2282.htm](http://www.jtbaker.com/msds/englishhtml/s2282.htm)

You'll notice that section 10, Stability and Reactivity, tells you that Silver Nitrate is stable. Of course, that means under normal room conditions (STP). You may need to read most MSDS with a large grain of salt. They scare the blazes out of you if you take them too seriously.
